Governance · role-based access

Role Architecture

The federation assigns base permissions by role and grants team, organization, and tournament capabilities within their scope. These roles and permissions are loaded from the live TUNESF database.

The Hierarchy

Who sits Where

Authority flows from the federation board down to the visitor. Higher roles inherit the capabilities of the tiers beneath them.

Roles in the database

The users table never hardcodes permissions. Each account holds one or more role keys, resolved through the RBAC layer on every request:

users.roles → VISITOR | PLAYER | CAPTAIN | REFEREE
                | TOURNAMENT_ADMIN | ORGANIZATION_OWNER
                | MODERATOR | PLATFORM_ADMIN | SUPER_ADMIN
Why RBAC — not hardcoded checks
  • Permissions are granted per role, so adding a role never means rewriting the platform.
  • One account can hold several roles — a captain can also be a referee for a lower division.
  • Separation of duties keeps competitive integrity: the referee who validates a result is never on either roster.
  • Every privileged action is written to the audit log, reviewed by platform admins.
